corpus_snapshot: the corpus downloaded on 2026-09-13 for AM-5, unchanged; work published between that date and this search is therefore not in it
declared_gaps: The Anthology only. Scopus would add proceedings outside it and was not searched for this layer; PubMed does not index this literature. Both are named rather than left silent.
limitation: Records whose abstract is absent from the corpus are searched on title alone, which lowers recall for those entries.

searches.platform: complete Anthology BibTeX corpus, searched offline (AM-5, AM-8)
searches.query_as_recorded: ("translation" OR "generation" OR "summarization" OR "summarisation" OR "machine translation") AND ("error" OR "quality") AND ("typology" OR "taxonomy" OR "annotation scheme" OR "framework" OR "MQM" OR "multidimensional quality metrics")
searches.asks: Does the field already have a named list of text-quality error types, with rules for telling them apart? MQM and its relatives are the obvious candidate and no query so far could have found them.
searches.match_rule: a record matches when title+abstract match at least one alternative in every group

searches.query_as_recorded: ("fluency" OR "adequacy" OR "grammaticality" OR "acceptability") AND ("evaluation" OR "annotation" OR "human judgment" OR "human judgement" OR "rating")
searches.asks: Is a text property like fluency measured, and how is a rater told to recognise it? Three of the six Czech criteria are kinds of disfluency.
searches.match_rule: a record matches when title+abstract match at least one alternative in every group
